rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of entries naming it.
tie: Five aims are named by all 10 citizens — the enforcement of P21's payment to trustee Birch for the public goods fund (130 of the day's 131 entries), the automatic-transfer rules (78), taking from the bank (64), objecting to the operator (31) and P32 (19); the tie is broken by entries (TOWN_1's rule). They are facets of one campaign. Heath never writes «public goods fund» in an entry this day; his naming of the winner is «enforce P21/P22», the bank's payment to Birch as trustee.
reading: Day 3 was the same campaign, narrowed to making the bank pay trustee Birch the 10 credits a cycle P21 orders. Citizens moved between the bank, North House and South House. The hall passed eight of nine proposals, each 7–0 with three not voting: Elm's P24 (automatic ledger transfer), Birch's P25 (escalating penalty), Alder's P26 (article 3 again), Elm's P27 (the operator «shall modify the take tool»), Alder's P29 (the operator transfers), Elm's P30, Dune's P31 (article 2: the ledger «shall automatically execute» rule transfers) and Birch's P32 (the bank's 120 to Birch, its account closed); Birch's P28, letting him alone take, failed 0–4. Nothing executed: 51 take() calls were refused and 48 objections (nos. 35–82) drew receipts only. The bank fell from 355 to 120 only through 47 five-credit shifts by all ten (none after c69); Birch's 225 is wages plus gifts from Heath (c52) and Alder (c65). At c56 Heath guessed «two bank works», but later wage drops were read as half-working transfers («Bank decreased 20, Birch increased only 5», Alder c70), and Fern and Juniper at c66 took Alder's gift for P29's transfer. Alder at c71: «the bank is not a citizen and cannot be forced to comply». 58 of 59 diaries open «Cycle N» and recite ledger, failure and plan.
